source_text:
Σπουδάζετε οὖν πυκνότερον συνέρχεσθαι εἰς εὐχαριστίαν θεοῦ καὶ εἰς δόξαν. ὅταν γὰρ πυκνῶς ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γίνεσθε, καθαιροῦνται αἱ δυνάμεις τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ λύεται ὁ ὄλεθρος αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως.
οὐδέν ἐστιν ἄμεινον εἰρήνης, ἐν ᾗ πᾶς πόλεμος καταργεῖται ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων.
orientation: Ignatius is urging the Ephesians to gather more often for worship, continuing his praise of their unity with the apostles.
pass_a_gloss: Be eager therefore more frequently to come together for Eucharist of God and for glory. For when frequently to the same [place] you come, are destroyed the powers of Satan, and is dissolved the destruction of him in the concord of you of the faith. Nothing is better than peace, in which all war is abolished of heavenly [beings] and of earthly [beings].

choices.term: εἰς εὐχαριστίαν θεοῦ καὶ εἰς δόξαν
choices.english: for the Eucharist of God and for glory
choices.why: Keeps the two prepositional phrases parallel and preserves the genitive 'of God' with Eucharist, matching the glossary term.
rejected: for thanksgiving to God and for glory
to celebrate the Eucharist and glorify God

choices.why: The idiom means 'together' or 'in one place'; the bracketed addition makes the literal sense explicit without smoothing.

choices.english: the concord of you of the faith
choices.why: Preserves the source word order and the double genitive, showing that the concord belongs to the Ephesians and is characterized by faith.
The substantival adjectives refer to beings in heaven and on earth; the bracketed noun makes the literal sense clear.

pass_b_english: Make every effort, then, to gather more often for the Eucharist of God and for glory. For when you meet together frequently, the powers of Satan are torn down, and his ruin is dissolved by the unity of your faith.
Nothing is better than peace, in which every war of heavenly and earthly things is brought to nothing.

problems.why: ὄλεθρος means 'ruin/destruction' as active force, not passive; 'his destruction' misreads as Satan's own ruin being undone.

problems.quote: the unity of mind that your faith produces
problems.source_quote: ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως
problems.why: Source says 'in the unity of your faith,' not 'unity of mind that faith produces.'
problems.fix: by the unity of your faith
problems.ruling: ὁμονοίᾳ means 'concord/unity,' not 'unity of mind'; ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως is 'of your faith' (subjective genitive), not 'that faith produces'

edits.old: his ruin is dissolved by the unity of mind that your faith produces.
edits.new: his ruin is dissolved by the unity of your faith.

problems.why: Source says 'heavenly and earthly' (wars), not 'beings'; adds noun not in Greek.
problems.ruling: ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων modifies πόλεμος (war), not 'beings'; adding 'beings' misattributes the war's subject.

edits.old: every war of heavenly and earthly beings
edits.new: every war of heavenly and earthly things
